subject: Third-party snapshot + planned region/operator changes — FinSight RFI
messages:
From: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@finsight.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: FinSight Security <security@finsight.com>, procurement@finsight.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Third-party operator snapshot + planned region changes (RFI)

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this. We're running a routine vendor risk refresh ahead of our Q1 procurement window and need a concise snapshot of Redwood's current third-party / operator footprint plus any planned region/operator changes that could affect residency or continuity. Our security team attached a short RFI template — we ask that you: 1) list all subprocessors/third parties that touch customer data (by role), 2) confirm cloud provider regions where you operate customer workloads for EU customers, and 3) flag any planned changes (operator rotation, region deprecation, new subprocessor onboarding) in the next 6 months.

Deliverables: roster CSV (template attached), a short note describing fallback/region-failover behavior, and any supporting docs (SOC2 report links, region change notices). Can you send an initial response by Friday PDT (2026-10-23)? If you prefer, we can also schedule a 30m walkthrough.

Thanks —
Marco Diaz
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
FinSight Capital

Attachment: FinSight_RFI_Template.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Third-party operator snapshot + planned region changes (RFI)

Hi Marco —

Appreciate the clear ask and the template. Looping in Rishi (Security Lead) and Marissa (Vendor Ops) to assemble the roster and the region notes. We'll populate the CSV and include the relevant SOC2 links and our standard region/fallback playbook.

Two quick clarifications:
- For "touch customer data" fields, do you want telemetry/observability vendors listed even if they only receive aggregated metrics?
- Should we include planned capability rollouts (e.g., dedicated capacity footprints) that are not region operator changes, or only items that impact where customer data is processed?

We aim to have a first-pass bundle to you by EOD Friday (PDT). If we need more time we'll let you know by Thursday.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

On Tue, Oct 20, 2026 at 10:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> Two quick clarifications: For "touch customer data" fields, do you want telemetry/observability vendors listed even if they only receive aggregated metrics?
> Should we include planned capability rollouts that are not region operator changes, or only items that impact where customer data is processed?

Hi all — quick answers from security:
- Please include telemetry/observability vendors if they receive any form of telemetry derived from customer workloads (even aggregated). We mark those with a separate data-sensitivity flag in the roster.
- For the immediate RFI, focus on vendors and operators that have the potential to impact data residency, access control, or recovery (so region/operator changes, new KMS/HSM providers, backups/replication partners). Planned product rollouts that don't change data processing locations or subprocessors can be summarized in a separate section but are lower priority.

Summary items we'll provide in the CSV and a short narrative:
- Current operators/subprocessors by role: cloud providers (AWS, GCP), dedicated pool operators (Redwood-managed), telemetry vendors, analytics vendors, identity/KMS, logging/alerts, backups, third-party model catalog providers.
- Region coverage: EU (eu-west-1, eu-west-3), US (us-west-2, us-east-1), APAC (asia-northeast1).
- Encryption/KMS: customer keys supported via KMS integrations; HSM-backed key support listed for Private deployments.
- Fallback: smart routing -> automatic fallback to compatible model variants in a different region; customers can pin region and receive SLA exceptions for cross-region failover.

I'll drop the populated roster CSV and a short change notice draft to the shared Drive link by EOD Thursday.

—Rishi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Third-party operator snapshot + planned region changes (RFI)

Hi Marco —

Attached is the initial roster CSV (redwood_thirdparty_roster_20261020.csv) and a short PDF notice that documents an operator rotation we plan for one EU edge operator. Short summary below:

- Planned change: retirement/rotation of a third-party EU edge operator (operator id: eu-edge-op-7) that currently supports some low-latency caching nodes.
- Effective date (planned): 2027-01-15 UTC. We expect zero data loss; the transition shifts affected traffic to an alternate operator within the same EU region and triggers automatic cache warm-up.
- Customer impact: customers who explicitly pinned to the operator id will be contacted via the Console and given a 30-day opt-out window; otherwise transparent failover applied.
- Mitigations: full configuration export, pre-warm KV caches, rollback window of 48 hours, and a post-migration audit with logs uploaded to the shared Drive link.

I've attached: cloud_region_deprecation_notice_20261022.pdf and the filled CSV. Also included links to SOC2 and the security attestations in the Drive folder.

Marissa Cole
Vendor Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_thirdparty_roster_20261020.csv; cloud_region_deprecation_notice_20261022.pdf

Hi Marissa / Kimberly —

Thanks — the CSV and the operator deprecation notice look good and answer our primary questions. A couple of follow-ups:

1) For the pin/opt-out flow, can you share the exact Console notification copy and the timeline you'll use? We want to ensure our operations team is aligned to accept opt-outs within your 30-day window.
2) We will upload your CSV into our vendor portal and run an automated mapping. If any additional evidence is required (e.g., an exported config or the post-migration audit logs), can we request those via a secure upload link?

Would also prefer a 30-minute walkthrough of the change plan the week of Nov 8; I'm available Tue 11/9 9–11am or Wed 11/10 1–3pm EST. Let me know which works and we'll send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Marco Diaz
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
FinSight Capital
